spans.s:
Vṛcayā is referred to once in the Rigveda as the spouse given by the Aśvins to kakṣīvant.
Foot notes i. 51, 3. Cf. Pischel, Vedische Studien, 1, 3, 203, who distinguishes two Kakṣīvants, but without sufficient reason, since i. 116, 17, must clearly refer to vṛcayā.

Vṛcīvant is the name of a tribe referred to once in the Rigveda, where it is clearly stated that the sṛñjaya king, daivavāta, conquered the turvaśa king and the Vṛcīvants. Zimmer thinks that the Vṛcīvants and the turvaśa people should be identified, but this is both unnecessary and improbable; it is adequate to assume that they were allied against the Sṛñjayas. The Vṛcīvants appear again only in the strange legend in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, according to which the Jahnus and the Vṛcīvants contended for sovereignty, viśvāmitra, the jahnu king, winning it by his knowledge of a certain rite. See also hariyūpīyā.
Foot notes vi. 27, 5 et seq.
